data.turoyo: <...> huwe w u aḥuno bəlḥuḏe nəfqiwo, təwriwo i ʕaskar. Šamʕəne Ḥanne w u Malke u aḥuno.
data.translation: <...> He and his brother would go out alone and break the army, Shamune Hanne and Malke, his brother.

rationale: First Infectum-wa/2 after round 1, with explicit army patient; correct reader I.1.

summary: New idiom: mətwər kef '(Detrans.) die Freude wird verdorben'

data.headword: mətwər kef '(Detrans.) die Freude wird verdorben'
data.turoyo: <...> omər aġaye mə i naqqa d kġulbitunne kuṯeli kef, d lo kmətwər kef diḏi.
data.translation: <...> Er sagte: Mein Agha, wenn ihr die Oberhand über sie gewinnt, empfinde ich Freude, wenn nicht, wird mir die Freude verdorben.

rationale: Affect noun plus breaking forms a collocation, not another numbered sense; lookup of twir/kef found no existing matching idiom.

summary: New idiom: lišono twiro 'sprachunfähig, nicht mehr sprechen könnend'

data.headword: lišono twiro 'sprachunfähig, nicht mehr sprechen könnend'
data.turoyo: <...> W kit zlam ǧamudo ʕal ḥaṣa, lišone twiro yo.
data.translation: <...> auf dem Rücken einen (vor Kälte) erstarrten Mann, der nicht mehr sprechen konnte (wörtl.: seine Zunge ist gebrochen).

rationale: One clear cold-induced speechlessness collocation; no physical tongue fracture is asserted and no matching twr idiom was found.

summary: New idiom: ʕayno twərto 'eingeschüchtert, ängstlich'

data.turoyo: W mu sabab d kətwayye ann emoṯaṯṯe dalil, taḥt i ḏ̣ulmiye nafiqi m sidux, ʕayne twərto.
data.translation: Und weil ihre Mütter unter der Tyrannei gedemütigt waren, sind sie dir mit gebrochenem Auge (als Angsthasen) entsprossen.

rationale: The literal eye phrase has a clear figurative interpretation in the edition; lookup found no matching idiom.

summary: New idiom: twəlle/towər ḥaṣo 'durch Reiten erschöpfen'

data.turoyo: L Ramazano məllele l Zaynal Bage: "Ya Zaynal Bage, twərxu haṣe daḥ ḥayewənani, ġalabe baṭilutu, ʕaǧizutu.
data.translation: Ramazan sprach zu Zeinal Bage: "Zeinal Bage, ihr habt diese Pferde müde geritten, ihr selbst seid sehr müde und erschöpft;

rationale: The affected back denotes exhausted mounts; record the bodily collocation rather than a separate verb sense.

summary: New idiom: twir ḥaṣo '(Detrans.) seinen Halt verlieren'

data.turoyo: "Alo, hano wa u sanadayḏan. Annaqla twir ḥaṣan!"
data.translation: "Wahrlich, dieser war unser halt; jetzt ist uns der Rückenzerbrochen."

rationale: The overt sanado makes the loss-of-support metaphor clear; distinct from literal fracture and the riding collocation.

summary: New idiom: twəlle/towər šar 'Unheil abwenden, das Böse brechen'

data.headword: twəlle/towər šar 'Unheil abwenden, das Böse brechen'
data.turoyo: Bas d azzi b Suriya ḥzeli, kəmḥalqi saḥne, kṭuwrənne, kowən daḥdoḥe, kəmmi: "Ṭwərlan u šar!"
data.translation: But when I went to Syria I saw that they throw plates, they break them, they become round pieces; they say: "We have broken the evil!"

rationale: Existing twr idioms and glossary search checked; round-1 D3 already covers nullifying evil, but this conventional ritual collocation is not listed. Literal plate-breaking and the quoted utterance make the distinction explicit.

summary: New idiom: twəlle/towər ġərur 'Hochmut unterdrücken'

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Əno i širayḏi, latyo təm mede! U nošo d lowe əšmo makixo, makəx ruḥe, ṭowər u ġərur...
data.translation: Father Brahim: My advice, there is nothing else! Unless a person is somewhat humble, humbles himself, breaks his arrogance...

rationale: No ġərur hit in the glossary lookup and no round-1 idiom; parallel makəx ruḥe establishes self-humbling. One attestation; list the noun construction as an idiom, not a numbered sense.

summary: Routine counts supplement the 124 fully supplied occurrences: Detransitive Preterit/1 and active Preterit/1 each have 35 routine tokens; Infectum/1 has 18. Counts are not extra decisions and do not replace examination of supplied verses.
Agent coding must follow Turoyo morphology: twirənne is active despite the German wording in Hors 1/69. EL 69 and EL 17 duplicate Hors contexts already in the entry; do not add them again.

Detransitive breaking includes intentional ritual effects (JTM 1.3/11), accidental breakage, military defeat, emotional states, honour and temporal thresholds. These functions cannot all be inferred from a German rendering alone.
Keep amro, xabro, lebo and nafšo as existing idioms. Infectum/5 at 42/12 is already cross-filed with the nafšo idiom; no new numbered self-control sense or duplicate example is proposed.

tworo remains in the inherited Detransitive Infinitiv section, even though 112/29 has an explicit active action and patients. Morphological section membership and semantic valency need editorial separation.
Uncertain personal harm in MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/13,15 and nəfus in PrS 6/34 are retained as provisional classifications, not selected as unambiguous examples.
No inherited gloss or source typography is silently normalized; odd strings such as 'Schlinge!' and 'Rückenzerbrochen' remain edition text.

Jan retains conversational interviews as well as written framing. Source ṭ for glossary t recurs in literal breaking, grief and language deficiency; it does not justify moving these tokens to the separate develop root ṭwr.

Preterit-wa forms twərwole and təwriwonne extend the aspectual inventory. Separated ṭwəri wo with plural morale and reduced Ṭwərwo may be Detransitive Preterit-wa, but copular/state readings are not resolved from these excerpts; neither is published as an unambiguous new-box example.

Food, stone, wood, bread and jug patients remain I.1. Round-1 Infectum/1 and physical Part. Pass./1 are already well represented; Jan thin-cell requests based on the unrevised entry are therefore mostly declined.

Ritual evil-breaking appears with finite active ṭwərlan, a bridal vessel context, and action noun ṭworo du šar. The inherited Detransitive Infinitiv filing of tworo is retained provisionally; it does not establish semantic Detransitive valency.

The amane reclassification is already a round-1 correction. The reader's complaint about Detransitive honour being under fruit sense 3 confuses the two independent numbering series: D3 already means nullification/disrespect. No new correction.
All source duplicates/repeated tokens receive separate occurrence decisions; a shared quotation is added once.
Does bare twīr with the feminine flask in MAC NE Unfortunate Youth/39 reflect agreement, an invariant exclamation or a repair? The two supplied tokens have separate decisions.
In PrS 6/34, does nəfus refer to people, authority or an administrative concept? The German 'Befehle' does not establish a defeat sense.
Confirm whether MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/13,15 describes beating or humiliation, and the reference of -llan in ktowaḷḷan.
Is čike twiro a conventional poverty expression, and is lišono twiro restricted to cold-induced speechlessness?
Should all tworo event nouns move out of the inherited Detransitive Infinitiv section? The clear twarte action noun has been moved to Nomen Actionis.
Confirm the fruit referent in 77/169; the supplied verse is anaphoric, although the reader assigns fruit-opening.
Does twir u lalyo strictly mean midnight has passed? 107/77 gives approximate ten/twelve o'clock alternatives.
The inherited Russian comment at 29/448 associates German Gesicht verlieren with loss of sight. The supplied verse supports social loss of face; delete or correct that comment editorially.
Jan 1.55/2626: is kṭuranne grape-crushing under twr or a form of ṭry 1 meaning leave? yaman does not resolve it. Analysis withheld from example selection.
Jan 2.12/3230: is matwəriwonne an actual stem III formation, an irregular/prothetic m- form, or a transcription problem? Almond-cracking is not a new sense; stem assignment is unresolved.
Jan 1.36/1468 and 2.33/5439: confirm Detransitive Preterit-wa versus a Part. Pass. plus past copula; reduced vowels and separated wo should not be normalized silently.
Jan 3.1/18: confirm təwrile active versus Detransitive before publishing this morphologically irregular backbone example.
Jan 2.4/889: confirm temporal twərle lu yawmo argument coding and the referent of aš šəqoṯo. The English rendering legs is not a reliable identification in a road-tamping passage.
Jan 1.46/1995 alternates raġli twiro yaho and raġli twərto yo within one verse: confirm agreement versus repair. No gender correction proposed.
Jan 2.5/1223: does not breaking each other mean mutual non-disavowal/concealing responsibility, rather than harm generally?

rationale: 'Amont' is a misspelling of the English preposition 'among' in this sentence.

summary: Physical breaking covers eggs, nuts, grain and buildings; these are participant extensions, not distinct craft senses. Donkeys can be agents (MAC Hanna Dewo/97).
Authority holders stand for their decisions (Bilgic); amane and səḥər extend nullification to an entrustment and a spell.

evidence.cite: Bilgic Die Rolle Məḏyaḏs im Tur Abdin/7

summary: Detransitive physical weakness in 66/344 concerns the person, not an overt noun 'strength'; the German supplies that noun. Active 6 has explicit ʕal ruḥe.
105/70 and 105/136 use 'year' for a complete set of dishes in wordplay. Treat the participant metaphor within breaking, not as ordinary time measurement.

Supports round-1 Detransitive 4: emotional lebi ṭwir and collective morale ṭwəri wo. No duplicate sense. faqire w ṭwire is compatible with general adversity and does not independently prove round-1 poverty sense 5.
Reciprocal ḥḏoḏe in an army concealing responsibility is provisionally mutual disavowal; the earlier refusal to name a companion aligns with I.4. Neither reciprocal object alone creates a new sense.
Breaking extends to social cohesion in ṭowər i ǧamaʕa; collective backbone destruction recalls the inherited backbone threat. No independent numbered sense is established.
